title: Closed support commutes with derived limits of sequences
statement:
Use the standing setting of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible: a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with their condensed coefficient conventions [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ its ring of integers. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_T))$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All sites and products use the fixed size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, and let $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Pullbacks are the coefficient-compatible module pullbacks [def-sfb-module-upper-star], and $Rj_*$ is the total right derived module direct image [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $G(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, with the adjunction unit as its map, and $R\underline\Gamma_Z=RG$, as in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. For a finite locally free $\Lambda_S$-module $L$ (on a pro-étale covering, $L$ is isomorphic to $\Lambda_S^{\oplus r}$ with finite ranks $r\ge0$ allowed to vary), consider
$$
j^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(V,\Lambda),\quad u^*:D(Z,\Lambda)\to D(S,\Lambda),\quad i^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(Z,\Lambda),\quad Rj_*:D(V,\Lambda)\to D(X,\Lambda),
$$
$$
R\underline\Gamma_Z=i^*\fib(\mathrm{id}\to Rj_*j^*):D(X,\Lambda)\to D(Z,\Lambda),\quad u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(S,\Lambda),\quad L[0]\otimes_{\Lambda_S}^{\mathrm L}-:D(S,\Lambda)\to D(S,\Lambda).
$$
Here $D(T,\Lambda)$ abbreviates the displayed pro-étale derived category; tensor is the derived tensor of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules], equivalently ordinary termwise sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] for this $L$. Each listed functor $F$ is additive and triangulated, preserves all small products, and preserves fibers, meaning that it carries distinguished fiber triangles to distinguished fiber triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. It commutes with sequential derived limits in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]: for every tower $(K_n,t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n)_{n\ge0}$, applying $F$ to any Roos triangle
$$
H\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow H[1],\qquad P=\prod_nK_n,\qquad \mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1},
$$
and identifying $F(P)$ with $\prod_nF(K_n)$ by the canonical product comparison yields a Roos triangle for $(F(K_n),F(t_n))$. In particular $F(H)$ is a derived limit of the image tower. Every comparison to another such derived limit that completes these product identifications to a morphism of Roos triangles is an isomorphism; no canonical choice between arbitrary triangulated-category cones is asserted.

proof.text: For open j and u identify the transported module pullback with upperStar by uniqueness of left adjoints. The exact open extension-by-zero adjunction derives to a right adjunction for the pullback. Thus both derived open restrictions preserve all existing products. The closed restriction product clause is the separate strictly smaller lemma lem-formal-closed-pullback-derived-products.

The derived open pullback/direct-image adjunction makes Rj_* a right adjoint. The existing formalClosedSupportAssertions.rightAdjoint makes RG a right adjoint to D(i_*). Both preserve products; composing with open u^* preserves them. Their additive right derived functors, and all exact pullbacks, are triangulated with the canonical shift instances.

Use condensed_dualizable_iff_proetale_cover. On the supplied trivializing cover, mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor and the coefficient-compatible pullback isomorphism identify the pullback of L[0] with the single complex of a finite free module. Single is additive, so this is a finite biproduct of single regular modules. The single tensor-unit comparison identifies each summand with the derived tensor unit. Prove finite biproducts of a dualizable object dualizable by induction, using the explicit Fin(n+1) splitting into a binary biproduct and the zero case. Descend the pairing by the locality theorem. The exact pairing supplies tensorLeftAdjunction, so L[0] tensor preserves products; the source derived tensor triangulated instance uses exactly derivedTensorObjCommShift.

For an additive triangulated F with products, prove F(towerTransitionEndomorphism f) ≫ e.hom = e.hom ≫ towerTransitionEndomorphism(Ff) by composing with every product projection. This explicitly uses preservation of subtraction, identity, and composition. Triangle.isoMk with components id,e,e identifies the image distinguished triangle with the image tower Roos triangle, including its connecting morphism. For any given compatible comparison psi to another Roos triangle, build Triangle.homMk with components psi,id,id and apply isIso₁_of_isIso₂₃. No cone choice or uniqueness assertion is introduced. Assemble the seven structures.

proof_origin.place: Product/fiber/Roos route retained; right adjunctions replace explicit K-injective product constructions, local dualizability replaces tensor descent.

split_report.summary: Replaced the imported uncited sketch by eight checked steps, reusing the existing restriction, K-injective, tensor and derived-product interfaces. No new nodes. Corrected the ordinary-triangulated-category natural-map wording to preservation of Roos triangles, as in the already reviewed parent unit, while retaining every listed functor, all small products and every tower. Local finite-free products and transition-map compatibility are proved explicitly.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q144-05413a78b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item in full. That is all eight steps, the statements of all 26 cited nodes, the unit, the blueprint main-20261015 statement and proof, and the Stacks sources 09AA, 0BK6, 08TC, 03DH and 03EL. The delivery only changes the status to split; the reviewed proof already existed. The statement is correct and keeps every target clause. The correction from 'natural map' to 'Roos triangles go to Roos triangles, and every completing comparison is invertible' is justified by 08TC, which gives derived limits only up to non-unique isomorphism; it is not a weakening. Steps 1–5, 7 and 8 check out against their cited statements. Step 3's direct computation of products of K-injectives avoids the blueprint's 'products of distinguished triangles' claim, which is not automatic. Long step 5 (2224 characters) is one argument and stays: L[0] is K-flat with flat terms, and the two derived-tensor bifunctors are identified by the uniqueness clause of the descent node together with lem-sfb-derived-monoidal. No existing comparison node was found. FIX (C1/C4): step 6 was marked elementary but used that restriction to a localized site commutes with the sheaf tensor product. In the DAG, sheafification is defined only by its universal property, and existing nodes cover only topological-space or Zariski opens, not S_proét. I added the statement-only node lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction (Stacks 03EL applied to the localization morphism of 03DH; unsplit; created.item = this item; same unit). Step 6 now cites it and also cites lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed for R^r⊗N ≅ N^r; it is no longer marked elementary, and proof_deps is recomputed. I accept all 15 declared tool_uses. There is no duplicate, no cycle and no SGA citation, and the edge cases hold (Z=X, Z empty, S empty, L=0, zero tower).
